effects: Sets the signer's wstETH allowance for spender_ to exactly amount_, replacing any previous allowance (ERC20Core.approve -> _approve).
An allowance of type(uint256).max is never reduced when spent (_spendAllowance returns early); any lower allowance is reduced by each transferFrom.
No tokens move and no native value is taken (not payable).
formats.shown: "Authorize spending" / "Allow to spend {amount} wstETH", with Spender and Amount fields; amounts at or above 2^255 show as "Unlimited wstETH".

findings.title: approve: the interpolated intent leaves out the spender, so the sentence does not say who may spend.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json approve interpolatedIntent "Allow to spend {amount_}". Case 0 sentence: "Allow to spend 250.5 wstETH". The spender only appears in the separate Spender field.

findings.title: approve: the Unlimited threshold is 2^255, but the code only treats type(uint256).max as an allowance that never decreases.
findings.evidence: ERC20Core._spendAllowance: `if (currentAllowance == type(uint256).max) { return; }`. descriptor.json approve Amount threshold "0x8000…0000", message "Unlimited".
findings.fix: You can set the threshold to 0xfff…fff (uint256 max). Values between the two cannot be spent in practice, so this is cosmetic.

findings.title: approve: Spender addressName types is limited to "contract", but the code accepts any non-zero address.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json approve Spender params.types ["contract"]. ERC20Core._approve only checks onlyNonZeroAccount(spender_).
findings.fix: Add "eoa" and "wallet" to types so EOA spenders still resolve.

effects: Moves amount_ wstETH from the signer to to_, with no fee (ERC20Core._transfer: _decreaseBalance(from_), balanceOf[to_] += amount_).
Reverts if to_ is the zero address or the balance is too low.
No native value is taken (not payable).
formats.shown: "Transfer wstETH" / "Send {amount} wstETH to {to}", with Recipient and Amount fields.

cases.notes: Mined on Arbitrum: 1.61 wstETH left the signer for 0x5ef0…9652. The screen shows exactly that, and the reader understood it.

formats.key: transferFrom(address from_, address to_, uint256 amount_)
effects: Spends amount_ of the allowance that from_ gave the signer (msg.sender); the allowance is not reduced if it is type(uint256).max (ERC20Core._spendAllowance).
Moves amount_ wstETH from from_ to to_. When from_ is the signer, this is the signer's own wstETH leaving.
No native value is taken (not payable).
formats.shown: "Transfer wstETH" / "Send {amount} wstETH to {to}", with Sender, Recipient and Amount fields.

findings.title: transferFrom: the interpolated intent leaves out from_, so it reads as if the signer sends its own tokens.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json transferFrom interpolatedIntent "Send {amount_} to {to_}". Case 3 sentence: "Send 0.113492582574591644 wstETH to 0x2aeD…1597", while the tokens come from 0x08b0…1e65 (the Sender field) and not from the signer 0xE66A…a346.

findings.title: transferFrom: the call uses up the signer's allowance from from_, and the screen does not say so.
findings.evidence: ERC20Core.transferFrom: `_spendAllowance(from_, msg.sender, amount_);`. No field or intent mentions the allowance.
findings.fix: This is what transferFrom means. Optionally write the intent as "Transfer wstETH using allowance".
